It’s our job to protect Americans while also advancing innovation. That’s why I'm joining @JayObernolte, @RepGuthrie, & @RepMMM to request additional information from the @FDA on policies to leverage health AI for patients.

Read the letter: https://t.co/iwry7wjfu1

President Trump’s celebration of the Right to Try Act in his nomination speech is a better roadmap for health care policy.

We should prioritize treatment for vulnerable Americans. This law provides federal protections so that certain unapproved drugs with potential lifesaving benefits can be administered to desperate terminally ill patients who have exhausted all FDA approved treatments. 

Discovering new breakthroughs requires balancing risk and innovation. It’s critical that future public policy ensures greater access to personalized medicine that doesn’t neatly fit current regulatory boxes. 

President Trump is already setting the right tone to secure America’s dominance in medical innovation. Under his leadership, the new policies I support—such as pathways for regenerative medicine, preventing government over-regulation of medical AI, and coverage policies for products that address unmet needs like PTSD and rare disease—will have a better chance of success.

We're taking a decisive step to unleash American energy innovation and restore market-driven competition. By enabling private, off-grid generation, we can support explosive load growth without straining existing grids—protecting ratepayers while powering the technologies that will define the future. Winning the AI race against China is not merely an economic priority; it’s a national security imperative, and the DATA Act gets us closer to that goal with smart policy that lets American industry lead.

Remember the ESG craze a few years ago?
 
Banks were scared to finance oil and gas. Bitcoin mining was supposedly boiling the oceans. Cow farts were destroying the planet.
 
That same anti-growth mentality has now shifted toward AI data centers.
 
Yes, they use enormous amounts of electricity. Fine, let’s figure out how to put more power on the grid. That’s what major technological revolutions require. And energy markets are already responding. Many data center companies want to build their own power sources and I have legislation that would streamline permitting to do that.
 
Yes, they use water for cooling. Mostly water that would otherwise flow out to sea.
 
In return? Trillions in private infrastructure investment. American jobs. AI leadership over China. Breakthroughs in medicine, engineering, and science.
 
America became powerful by building things. We shouldn’t start apologizing for it now.

I’ve been warning about the threat of drone attacks to the homeland for years. It’s not a matter of if our adversaries decide to exploit this gap, but when. If we continue to standby while watching the world around us adapt to the next frontier of threats then we’re setting ourselves up for a catastrophic failure. 
 
The reality is, we approach this problem the wrong way. People think about it as a Russia-Ukraine style drone mobilization led by warfighters but some teenager in his room with access to ChatGPT could carry something like this out NOW. 
 
The threat’s already here, it’s not hypothetical. We need to arm our critical infrastructure to defend itself.
 
From the latest episode of Hold These Truths with defense expert Dr. Seth Jones.

The first battle in the War on Terror was on Flight 93, when forty Americans made the decision to fight back against evil. Today I visited the Flight 93 National Memorial in Shanksville, PA.

It’s an incredible place, and reminds us how quickly ordinary people can become heroes. From the moment they were hijacked to the moment they fought back was only 29 minutes. These brave Americans made the decision to fight for their lives in only 29 minutes.

Twenty-five years later, the threats to our homeland look different—cyberattacks, drones, AI, foreign espionage, and adversaries exploiting gaps in our security.

We cannot wait for another catastrophe to remind us what complacency costs. We have to recognize these threats and act before Americans pay the price again.

President Trump is right. China would absolutely love for America to talk itself out of building the infrastructure necessary to dominate AI. In fact, they’re already running influence operations to encourage exactly that.

Politicians who join the anti-data center frenzy aren’t showing leadership. They’re doing China’s work for them.

Xi and the Chinese Communist Party could not have designed a better psyop campaign to stop American AI data centers than the one critics on the left and right are running themselves.
 
The country that leads in AI will have the global advantage in defense, science, manufacturing, and economic growth for decades to come. America risks regulating itself into poverty and irrelevance if we continue down this path.
 
The debate is being framed as a false choice by critics: halt all development or ignore every risk. We should do neither.
 
Make it easier to build AI data centers. Expand the electric grid. Require developers to pay for the power, water, and infrastructure they need. 
 
President Trump is right on this issue, and more leaders in tech and government should have the courage to make the same case instead of caving in to public fear.
 
If America refuses to build the future here, the future will be built somewhere else.
